      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name

          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create, the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept
            when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and
            brackets are stripped. The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the
            '+'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted the server sets it to its current
            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Create-only flag. When true, the owner is allowed to be created even
            though another owner already has the same last name and address (for
            example, family members living together). Defaults to false.
          type: boolean
          default: false
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone

  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type

          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"

          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id

    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create, the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept
            when present, otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single
            leading '0' is dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and
            brackets are stripped. The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the
            '+'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted the server sets it to its current
            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Create-only flag. When true, the owner is allowed to be created even
            though another owner already has the same last name and address (for
            example, family members living together). Defaults to false.
          type: boolean
          default: false
          writeOnly: true
          example: false

## What I changed

The `sharesHousehold` opt-in and its rejection path already existed; the missing piece was the `householdId` — assigning a stable shared identifier and returning it. I wired that through the full stack:

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `householdId` string property to the `Owner` schema (so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct maps it automatically). `sharesHousehold` stays `writeOnly` on `OwnerFields`.

2. **`model/Owner.java`** — added a `householdId` field (`@Column(name = "household_id")`) with getter/setter.

3. **DB schemas** — added a `household_id` column to the `owners` table in all four `schema.sql` files (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres). The tests run under the `hsqldb` profile with `ddl-auto=none`, so the SQL column is what actually matters for them.

4. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — added `assignHousehold(...)`, called during `addOwner`. When `sharesHousehold` is true and at least one existing owner matches the same last name + address (using the same case-/whitespace-insensitive normalization as the existing duplicate check):
   - It reuses an existing member's `householdId` if one is present, otherwise derives a stable one from the normalized last name + address (first 12 upper-case hex chars of SHA-256).
   - It stamps that id onto the new owner **and** back-fills any matching member that lacks it, so the whole household stays consistent.
   - If the flag is absent, or set but no household exists, no id is assigned.

## How it satisfies the spec

In the acceptance test, owner `a` is created normally; `b` and `c` then join with `sharesHousehold=true` at `a`'s name/address. `b` triggers generation of the id (also back-filled onto `a`); `c` reuses it — so `b` and `c` report the same non-blank `householdId`, which is what the test asserts. The pre-existing 409 behavior for duplicates *without* the opt-in is untouched.
